Thanks for the demo earlier — appreciate the clear walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and asks so we can move to a short evaluation sprint: 

- Goal: launch an internal support assistant (search + short generated replies) for early beta (10k daily active queries).
- Key constraints: sub-200ms 95p latency for read-only search path; generated responses can tolerate up to ~400ms 95p.
- Budget target (pilot): ~$5k/month.

We recorded the session and attached a small sample of queries we expect to be high-volume (attachment: cobble_sample_queries.csv).

Can you send your recommended shortlist (3 models), quick rationale for cost/latency/quality tradeoffs, and a plan for a 2-week evaluation (what we need to provide, expected gates)? Also please include any prompt sets / test harness you recommend so we can reproduce the checks.

Thanks — can we aim to have the shortlist and gating checklist tomorrow?

Thanks Aditi — good context and the sample queries are really helpful. Attached: benchmark_summary_COB-4821.pdf and an initial prompt pack (cobble_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl). Below is a recommended "inference trio" with concise rationale and the gating checklist for a 2-week sprint.

Recommended shortlist (prioritized):

1) Redwood-compact-quant (cost-optimized)
   - Why: best token/unit economics at lower sequence lengths; quantized path we run has ~40% lower cost vs fp16.
   - Expected 95p latency: ~260ms (single-request, continuous-batching off); can be pushed to ~180ms with aggressive KV-prefix caching for autocomplete-heavy queries.
   - Quality: solid for short answer extraction and paraphrase; may hallucinate on open-ended generative tasks — use for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) answer synthesis with stricter guardrails.

2) OpenFlare-large (quality-first)
   - Why: highest factuality and instruction-following in our LLM catalog for customer-facing replies.
   - Expected 95p latency: ~420ms (higher compute), cost ~2.5x Redwood-compact-quant.
   - Quality: recommend for final response stages where tone and precision matter; pair with fast model as pre-filter.

3) Goliath-8B-rt (low-latency hybrid)
   - Why: best latency tail for short completions; favorable for interactive flows where strict 95p SLO is required.
   - Expected 95p latency: ~140–200ms.
   - Quality: slightly behind OpenFlare on hallucination metrics but acceptable for short, templated customer replies.

Quick tradeoff summary:
- Cost: Redwood-compact-quant < Goliath-8B-rt < OpenFlare-large.
- Latency: Goliath-8B-rt < Redwood-compact-quant (with caching) < OpenFlare-large.
- Quality: OpenFlare-large > Goliath-8B-rt > Redwood-compact-quant.

Gating checklist for 2-week evaluation (what we will run):
- 0) Access: we need a test API key and a small, dedicated quota for COB-4821. (We can provision a short-lived key after NDA/ToU — see NDA link.)
- 1) Baseline benchmarks: run our provided sample queries across the three models (attached harness + benchmark_summary).
- 2) Latency SLOs: validate 95p under your expected concurrency (we'll run 50 concurrent workers targeting ~10 RPS).
- 3) Quality tests: run the prompt pack (attached) and evaluate MRR / hallucination rate on the 150-case prompt set.
- 4) Regression checks: we’ll set up simple exact-match and keyword-coverage alerts; if hallucination rate increases by >6% vs baseline we flag for manual review.
- 5) Ops plan: recommend canary rollout sequence — warm Goliath-8B-rt for live reads, degrade to Redwood-compact-quant for bulk async tasks; OpenFlare-large for post-edit/finalization.

Attachments & links:
- benchmark_summary_COB-4821.pdf (attachment) — concise perf/cost table from our internal runs.
- cobble_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl (attachment) — 150 labeled prompts/tests.
- Live snapshot: https://redwood-internal.s3/benchmarks/COB-4821/snapshot.html (read-only for Cobble link will be enabled).
- Drive folder with reproducible scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_benchmark

Next steps / asks from Cobble:
- Confirm NDA (I attached a short form) and allow us to provision the test key.
- Share expected concurrency profile (per-minute QPS distribution) so we size the quota correctly.
- Quick sync: 30 minutes tomorrow to confirm test matrix and times for a first run?

If that all looks reasonable I’ll spin up the trial environment and drop the keys to the thread.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

+1 to Hannah's trio. One operational note: add Goliath-small as a warm fallback for sub-100ms cache-miss replies — cheaper than Goliath-8B-rt and closes a lot of tail cases.

Estimated pilot run-rate (rough):
- Redwood-compact-quant baseline: ~$2.3k/mo at 100k tokens/day profile.
- Goliath-8B-rt warm layer (light traffic): add ~$1.6k/mo.
- OpenFlare-large (sporadic): depends on final mix but ballpark +$2–3k/mo if used for ~20% of responses.

I can add a short cost simulation in the Drive folder this afternoon.

—Ben
